text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- An estimated two thousand people demonstrated in front of the Kaunas municipal government, protesting against bad economic conditions.
- Accepting an invitation from President Algirdas Brazauskas, United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan said he would visit Lithuania when his schedule allowed. No specific date was mentioned.
- A Lithuanian mission to NATO will be established on August 1, replacing the present NATO relations bureau.

- Lithuania will grant refugee status for the first time under the 1951 United Nations Convention on Refugee Status in August. The convention went into effect on July 27. Lithuania has more than 40 applicants for refugee status.

- Lithuania's securities commission is expected on Friday to register the 22.85 million litas share capital of 21.5 percent state-owned brewer Utenos Gerimai following a legal dispute over the shares that was decided in favour of Utenos.
- The finance ministry has received offers from seven banks to grant Lithuania a $100 million syndicated loan.
- On Friday the securities commission is expected to register Lithuanian Savings Bank's 20 million litas share capital boost. The increase will take the bank up to 66 million litas share capital.
- The Lithuanian government has abolished export limitations on grain and grain products due to oversupply. This year's harvest is expected to be 2.6-2.8 million tonnes.

- Hermis Bank on Tuesday presented its global depository receipts in New York, which carry a nominal value of eight million litas after the Bank of Lithuania on Friday registered its share captial increase. Its share capital now totals 90 million litas.
- The government decided to speed up the restitution of land, by obligating districts to process applications for restitution by August 15. The land should be surveyed by September 1.
